newsitem.title: UK: BP shares strong as results beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BP shares strong as results beat forecasts.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum Co Plc rose sharply after it reported first quarter results which beat analysts' forecasts in all its sectors of operation.
BP shares were up 26 pence, or 3.7 percent, at 729-1/2 by 1120 GMT after being quoted around 713 just before the results announcement.

"The results are very good...better in every segment," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding. "It's important to note that it's not just (higher) oil prices -- it's also refining and chemicals."
BP reported net earnings before expectional items of a record 755 million stg, up 19 percent on a year earlier and ahead of forecasts centered around 690 million.
Fergus MacLeod, analyst at Natwest Markets, said the results reflected a good performance from the upstream oil and gas exploration and production division.
But he said they also contained "better progress towards self-help objectives," referring to BP's cost-cutting and efficiency drive.
The company said its improving portfolio of assets, continuing focus on costs and reduced level of debt were lowering the impact of changes in prices and margins.

"...the continuing level of underlying performance and new business activity keeps progress towards achievement of the medium term targets ahead of schedule," BP said in an outlook accompanying the results.
BP's chief executive John Browne has set a 1997 objective of achieving $300 million of underlying performance improvements from productivity gains and cost savings.
Kleinwort's Spedding said the results would prompt those anlaysts who were more cautious in their BP estimates to raise forecasts for 1997.
